what: AutoZone sells car parts and accessories through nearly 8,000 stores in the United States, Mexico and Brazil. Alongside walk-in customers it supplies repair garages, which is its faster-growing business.
customers: People repairing their own cars, and professional repair shops buying parts for same-day delivery.
money: parts, batteries, oil and accessories sold in store
parts delivered to independent repair garages
moat: Store density and distribution that put almost any part within hours of a mechanic, which a part sold online next day cannot match.
risks: Debt of about $13 billion against almost no cash, because it borrows to buy back shares
It pays no dividend, returning cash only through buybacks
Mexican and Brazilian expansion carries currency risk
Electric vehicles need fewer replacement parts over time
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 29% is exceptional for a retailer
The average age of cars on American roads keeps rising, which raises repair demand
Commercial sales to garages are growing faster than the retail side
watch: Same-store sales growth, especially in the commercial business.
